data.name: Adonias
data.long_meaning: Adonias is a Hebrew name derived from the Hebrew word 'adon' meaning 'lord' or 'master'. In the Bible, Adonias is the name of a son of King David. After the death of King David, Adonias attempted to usurp the throne, but Solomon, another son of David, ultimately succeeded.

data.cultural_impact: Adonias represents the pursuits of power and desire for reign, even against family and moral principles. His name serves as a reminder that wealth, status, and familial relation cannot replace the values of justice, morality, and rightful claim to the throne.
data.spiritual_significance: Adonias symbolizes the inner struggle between desire and morality, between power and humility, and ultimately, between worldly ambition and God's will. It serves as a reminder that true strength and power come not from earthly possessions or position, but from whatever is within us spiritually. Adonias' story highlights the importance of humility, obedience, and seeking the best for others above personal gain.

historical_references.reference: Adonias was the eldest surviving son of King David of Israel and Haggith, the wife of David taken from the wife of Absalom. Adonias attempted to usurp the throne of his father, but was killed by Solomon, who had succeeded David. (1 Kings 1:5-13, 1:18-27)
historical_references.context: During the reign of King David of Israel, Adonias, the eldest surviving son of David by Haggith, attempted to seize the throne for himself after David's death. He was supported by Joab, the commander of the army, and Abiathar, the priest. However, Solomon, another son of David, who was favored by his father, learned of the plot and took action to secure the throne. Adonias was killed in the resulting confrontation.

historical_references.reference: Adonias, the son of King David, was a man of great beauty and charm. He was favored by his mother, Haggith, and by Joab, the commander of the army. When King David grew old, Adonias made a feast for all the king's sons and the royal court. He invited Absalom, who was also a contender for the throne, but excluded Solomon, the rightful heir. (1 Kings 1:5-6, 1:9-10)
historical_references.context: Adonias, the eldest surviving son of King David by Haggith, was known for his great beauty and charm. He was favored by his mother and by Joab, the commander of the army, who saw him as a potential successor to David. When David grew old and weak, Adonias held a grand feast for all the king's sons and the royal court. He invited Absalom, who was also a contender for the throne, but deliberately excluded Solomon, the rightful heir. This was a clear power grab and an attempt to seize the throne for himself.
